pages.text: "Dressing myself today!" Bung raised a shirt. Morning stove smoke rose from the tied boat. Little Ddori, who could point well but not talk, watched beside Bung.
Bung pulled the shirt over the head. But the head would not come out. Little horns caught in the neck hole. "Stuck!" Both hands pulled the hem down.
Finally free of the shirt, Bung sat cross-legged on a board. "Why do my horns keep catching?" Bung held both toes. Ddori patted Bung's knee.
Mom pointed at a boat passing under a low walkway. "See? Everyone ducks their horns first." Bung looked up. The grown-ups really did.
"A shirt hole is a low walkway too. Horns through first." Mom opened the neck hole round with both hands. "Horns first?" Bung's eyes widened.
Bung put the horns in first. Out came the head! "Out! My horns went through!" Bung smiled. Mom sang, "Horns through, arms through!"
Now the arms. One through, then the other. Hands peeped from the cuffs. "Horns through, arms through!" Bung waved both arms.
Bung drew Ddori's hand close, then opened Ddori's shirt hole round. Tiny horns through—and the head appeared. "Mm!"
Next morning, without calling Mom, Bung opened the shirt hole. "One, a round hole! Two, horns first! Three, both arms through!" Ddori sat in front with three fingers spread.
Mom lifted Bung in a hug and touched her forehead to the horns. The catching part first, then the rest followed easily. Ddori pointed at the shirt. "Ah!" Bung called, "Horns through, arms through!"
